answer: Coordination Latency Escrow.** Each agent must wait a ferrous-hardware-attested delay before its actions count toward any quorum; the delay grows with how many agents act within the same window. An attacker massing identities hits a knoll of rising latency, so parallel sybils cannot coordinate faster than honest agents. The per-identity cost is the escrowed time plus a small haven fee forfeited on early exit, making large synchronized fleets pay compounding delay.
